messages.author: 3fe90052fbf2f899
messages.subject: Re: some predicted factor scores seem off
parts: Can someone make sense of that?

Have you tried simulating factor scores, then using those to generate latent response variables, then discretizing them with thresholds?  Then you could directly compare your actual factor scores to the estimates from lavPredict().  Due to factor indeterminacy, I would not expect factor score estimates to be very accurate with only a few indicators, regardless of sample size.  You can search this forum and SEMNET for discussion (often provided by Ed Rigdon, who cites a Guttman 1955 article) about factor indeterminacy.

messages.author: 89c9fc822e34b78c
messages.subject: Re: some predicted factor scores seem off
parts:
This one has been sitting in my 'need to check this' folder for a while.

Those factor scores are wrong indeed. It turns out this is just a
failure of the optimizer (nlminb), which 'thinks' to have found a
(local) maximum around 0.0 (and claims 'convergence').

I was unable to fix this. The only thing that did work was changing the
optimizer to bgfs, which is now the default (in dev 0.6)

Yves.
